info.text:
No credit history means no credit card? That's a myth.

The CFPB's corrected June 2025 estimate: about 7.0 million US adults (2.7%) had no credit file in December 2020, down from 5.8% in 2010.
Secured cards, student cards, authorized-user status and credit-builder loans are built for people starting from zero.
Example: a $200 deposit on a secured card usually means a $200 limit; 30% of $200 is $60, the point Experian says utilization starts to weigh more.
myFICO: a FICO Score needs an account at least 6 months old, reported within the past 6 months. Under 21, card rules require your own income or assets, or a co-signer 21+ (many issuers don't accept co-signers).

Sources: CFPB (June 2025), myFICO, Experian, Regulation Z 1026.51.
News and education, not financial advice.
